resources.string: Let the agent use apps on this phone within the scope you choose. Off by default; you turn it on yourself.
Phone control is an experiment and isn\'t turned on in this build.
Let the agent use apps on this phone
The agent can tap, swipe and type in an app you choose. You can set a time limit or choose Permanent, and pause, take over or end the task at any time.
The whole on-device runtime is trusted: any program or agent running in it can use this connection, not only the chat you\'re in.
Wireless debugging gives device-level access. While it\'s connected, whatever holds the connection can do far more than this screen allows. Turn wireless debugging off when you\'re done.
What\'s on the chosen app\'s screen, including text and screenshots, may be sent to the AI model the chat uses.
Confirming in this app records your choice. It can\'t prove that a person tapped it, since software controlling the phone could tap it too.
Off by default. Turning it off ends any task and disconnects.
Turning it off ends the task and disconnects.
In Developer options, turn on Wireless debugging. The phone must be on Wi-Fi.
Already paired. Pair again only if connecting fails.

Tap the button below. AndChamber opens the wireless debugging screen and looks for this phone\'s pairing dialog by itself. There, tap \"Pair device with pairing code\" and keep that dialog open. You only type the six-digit code, in AndChamber\'s notification.
Enter the code in the notification
Keep the pairing dialog open, pull down the notification shade and type the six-digit code into AndChamber\'s notification. Don\'t paste it into a chat.
Looking for the pairing dialog on this phone…
On the wireless debugging screen, tap \"Pair device with pairing code\" and keep the dialog open. Once it\'s found, the notification asks only for the six-digit code.
On some Xiaomi phones, the notification only shows its text box after you long-press it.
No open pairing dialog was found in time. Make sure wireless debugging is on and the \"Pair device with pairing code\" dialog is open, then search again.
No wireless debugging connection was found in time. Make sure wireless debugging is on, then search again.
The phone didn\'t allow the search. Check that Wi-Fi is on, then search again, or enter the port yourself.
AndChamber won\'t guess which one is right. Close other pairing dialogs and search again, or enter the port yourself.
The pairing notification can\'t be shown. Turn on notifications, or pair manually below if the dialog can stay open.
This only works while the pairing dialog stays on screen, for example in split screen. The code is never saved.
From the pairing dialog, not the port on the wireless debugging screen.
Six digits from the pairing dialog.
AndChamber looks for this phone\'s own wireless debugging port and connects to it. Nothing to type. Connecting doesn\'t let the agent do anything yet.
Looking for wireless debugging on this phone…
Search again, or enter the port from the wireless debugging screen yourself.
Pair first. After pairing succeeds, AndChamber tries to connect on its own.
Use the port under \"IP address & port\" on the wireless debugging screen. It differs from the pairing port and changes whenever wireless debugging restarts.
From \"IP address & port\" on the wireless debugging screen.
IP address or host name, without a port.
Enter an IP address or host name without a port.
Turn it on in Developer options, then try again.
Wireless debugging needs a Wi-Fi connection.
The code was wrong or has expired. Open a new pairing dialog and use its new code.
Keep the pairing dialog open and try again. Its port changes every time the dialog opens.
Check that wireless debugging is still on, then search again or enter the port yourself. If you haven\'t paired yet, pair first.
The phone hasn\'t approved this connection
Wireless debugging may have turned off, or the Wi-Fi changed. Connect again.
See Details for the technical message, then try again.
The agent can\'t use phone control yet
The phone tool isn\'t loaded in the running OpenChamber, so the task was cancelled and nothing was done in the app. Restart OpenChamber from Home, then set up the task again.
Nothing was started. Unlock the phone, then set up the task again.
Nothing was started. It may have been removed or blocked. Choose an app from the list.
Nothing was granted. Check the connection and the settings above, then try again yourself. See Details for the technical message.
This says nothing about actions taken earlier; check the app if unsure. See Details for the technical message.
Restart OpenChamber to use phone control

OpenChamber on this phone is running, but it started before phone control was available, so the agent can\'t use it yet. Go Home and restart OpenChamber. Restarting interrupts tasks running in OpenChamber.
OpenChamber on this phone isn\'t running, so the agent can\'t use phone control. Go Home and start it.
What you filled in is kept. You can allow the task once OpenChamber is ready.
Can\'t start: no way to pause from other apps
Notifications for AndChamber are off, so the Pause control can\'t be shown while another app is in front. Turn notifications on, then check again.
The phone control notification category is turned off. Turn it on in notification settings, then check again.
AndChamber couldn\'t confirm that you can pause the agent from other apps. Check again. If this keeps happening, do the task yourself.
The agent asked to use an app
It suggested the task below. You choose the app, the time and the actions. Nothing starts until you confirm.
The agent can act only in this app. The list of apps stays on this phone and isn\'t sent to the model.
%1$d system, settings or AndChamber apps can\'t be chosen and aren\'t listed. Search for one to see why.
No app on this phone can be chosen. System and settings apps aren\'t supported.
System and settings apps can\'t be chosen.
What should the agent do? You\'ll see this while it works.
When time runs out, the agent pauses. It never extends its own time.
Supported ASCII characters only; no Unicode, passwords, or automatic submission.
Reading the screen is always included, so the agent can see what it\'s doing.
The task description is too long.
Wait for the current step to finish.
You can pause, take over or end the task at any time, here or from the notification.
Confirming records your choice in this app. It doesn\'t prove who tapped it.
It pauses by itself when time runs out, when you come back to AndChamber, or when the app leaves the screen or can\'t be confirmed.
It never extends its own time. More time needs your confirmation.
No new actions are accepted. The agent\'s last action hasn\'t finished yet and may still take effect. You don\'t need to press Pause again.
Pausing… waiting for the last action to finish
An action is running now. If you pause, it may still finish.
The agent\'s new action was refused
Its previous action hasn\'t finished. Nothing was queued, and nothing needs to be pressed.
Still working on the previous step
Your last tap wasn\'t applied because a step is still running. Wait for it to finish before trying again.
No new actions are accepted, but the last action may still take effect. Check %1$s before deciding what to do next.
You marked the last action as checked. No new actions are accepted.
the Pause control is no longer available
Continuing asks you to confirm again with a new time limit. Nothing renews by itself.
Connect again below before continuing. Connecting doesn\'t restart the agent; you still confirm here.
Every step was read back from the app and matched.
Some steps couldn\'t be confirmed. Check them in the app.
Nothing here was confirmed in the app. A tool reporting success doesn\'t mean the step worked.
No verified results are recorded here. Check the target app or the conversation.
Result unknown · check in the app
Only while the agent is working in the chosen app. Coming back to AndChamber ends that access, so the screen isn\'t read from here.
Settings, permission, password or payment apps can\'t be chosen.
Set this up once: choose the apps the agent may use, what it may do, and for how long. Then just ask in the local OpenChamber chat. Requests inside this scope start without asking here each time.

Say what you want in the local OpenChamber chat, for example which app and what to do. You won\'t be sent here to approve each task. Tasks follow your chosen scope and time limits. Permanent removes time expiry, not the other stop rules.
The running OpenChamber started before phone control was set up, so the chat can\'t use the phone yet. Restart it once; your chats are kept.
This stops and starts the local OpenChamber so it loads the phone tool. Your chats are kept, but a reply in progress is interrupted.
The chat can use the phone once the tool is confirmed loaded.
Start it from Home. Your scope is kept.
It isn\'t confirmed that OpenChamber loaded the phone tool. Until it is, the chat can\'t use the phone.
Your scope is kept, but the agent can\'t act until wireless debugging is connected again.
Scope ends in %1$d min · each task up to %2$d min
Typing passwords, codes or payments is never done for you. If the agent asks for you, it stops and waits.
Up to %1$d apps. Installed apps and ordinary preinstalled ones can be chosen; settings, permission, password and payment apps can\'t.
%1$d apps can\'t be chosen and aren\'t listed. Search for one to see why.
There is no time limit, but it still pauses when you take over, come back to AndChamber, lock the screen, the connection drops, or the app leaves the screen or can\'t be confirmed.
Each task: no limit of its own, ends when the scope ends
Scope: permanent. It doesn\'t end by time; turn it off here when you\'re done.
Each task: no limit of its own. It still ends when the scope ends.

Permanent only means it doesn\'t end because time runs out. Taking over, locking the screen, a dropped connection or turning phone control off still stops the agent. After AndChamber or the phone restarts, an old task doesn\'t resume by itself. Each single action still has its own timeout.
You trust the whole local OpenChamber runtime with this scope, not only one chat. You can turn it off here at any time.
For %1$d h; each task up to %2$d min.
Chat requests inside this scope start without asking here. Pause, take over and end stay available in the notification and overlay.
The agent looks at the screen again first and continues inside your scope. Nothing it did before is re-sent. The chat is told to carry on.
Do that step yourself, then continue here. The agent doesn\'t see what you type.
The chat was told to continue
Follow it in the chat or the overlay.
The continuation result couldn\'t be confirmed. Check the phone and the chat; nothing was re-sent.
The task\'s access is active again, but the chat wasn\'t told to continue, and nothing was re-sent. Open the chat to see where it stands, or pause or take over if you don\'t want it to act.
Available once the stop is confirmed.
Check the last action in the app first.
Available once chat use is ready (see above).
This app isn\'t in your scope. Change the scope first.

Your setup is kept: no need to pair again or set the scope again. Confirm Resume chat use here, or use the card above to continue a stopped task. Phone requests from the chat are refused until you confirm.
Chat use is also paused. Fixing this doesn\'t resume it; you resume it here afterwards.
The agent asked for you, so it stopped.
You took over the phone, so the agent stopped.
It isn\'t known whether the last step took effect, so the agent stopped.
The connection or the stop entry dropped, so the agent stopped.
The screen was locked, so the agent stopped.
The local OpenChamber restarted, so the agent stopped to be safe.
The chat can then start new tasks inside the scope you saved. This doesn\'t start a task by itself, doesn\'t re-send anything done before, and doesn\'t change the scope or its time limits.
A stopped task is waiting. Continue or end it in the card above.
Available once the current task is over.
A step may already have taken effect and hasn\'t been checked yet. Check the last result first; this entry won\'t clear the pause automatically.
The agent is waiting for you

It stopped in %1$s and asked you to do one step yourself; it took no further steps. When you\'re done, tap the button below and the same task carries on. No need to pair again or set the scope again. The agent doesn\'t see what you type.
Waiting for you · you\'re in control
I\'m done, let the agent continue…
The agent didn\'t get access back and nothing was re-sent. The task stays here; you can confirm continue again once the reason is fixed.
Chat use wasn\'t ready at that moment.
Your saved scope no longer allows it.
The stop entry couldn\'t be shown.
The task\'s app couldn\'t be brought back.
The page kept changing, so no stable screen hierarchy was available. This alone does not mean the connection dropped.
Reading the screen again took too long.
The screen kept changing while it was read.
The phone-control connection is no longer available.
It was cancelled by a newer change.
The last continue is still being handled.
This stop was already continued, and the chat is told only once. Look in the chat.
The original task is gone. After resuming, ask in the chat to start a new one.
